extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants (R01/R21) and principal investigators writing to the new 12-page format
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and community-sourced heuristics for converting traditional NIH R01/R21 proposals into the shortened 12-page (R01) / 6-page (R21) format, including where to place methods, preliminary data, and justifications across form sections. Emphasizes practical tradeoffs and reviewer expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to the 12-page limit; be concise and clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the proposal within the new shorter page limits (R01 meat reduced to 12 pages; R21 to 6 pages). The shorter format forces clarity, concision, and straight-forward presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on main arguments and high-value content; omit lengthy, nonessential detail. Several commenters reported it was as easy to convey the same preliminary data in the shorter format by removing detailed methods and extraneous citations. Treat the limits as a feature that improves 'punch' and readability rather than a bug.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on 'cheating' by hiding core content in other sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid intentionally moving essential experimental details or arguments out of the page-limited Research Strategy into other administrative sections to circumvent the page limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may notice and penalize 'cheating' (one commenter described losing about a point for this). NIAID and other agency guidance may flag this practice. If you do move material, be cautious: some reviewers won't find it and may react negatively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Vertebrate Animals section for detailed animal methods and justifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Place detailed animal-specific methods, statistical justifications for animal numbers, species/strain choices, doses, inoculation details, and similar content in the Vertebrate Animals section when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is commonly done and can be appropriate because the Vertebrate Animals section explicitly asks for species/strain/number justification. However, write the main text so that a reviewer can understand the experimental design without needing to read that section; otherwise you risk reviewers missing key details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage Facilities & Other Resources / Equipment sections to describe pertinent capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Facilities & Other Resources and Equipment statements to describe how the scientific environment, physical resources, and major equipment contribute to the probability of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The solicitation wording ('ways in which the proposed studies will benefit from unique features' and 'pertinent capabilities') provides an opening to describe not only equipment but also how those capabilities support the proposed studies — potentially including concise data or preliminary results that demonstrate relevance. Be judicious; don't place core study rationale solely here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place preliminary data strategically in Approach/Significance as rationale for aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate preliminary studies into the Approach (or distribute between Significance and Approach) to show feasibility and to serve as a rationale for each specific aim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only include preliminary data that are directly applicable to the proposed experiments; this reduces length and keeps the reviewer focused. Several commenters recommend using prelims as part of the rationale for each aim rather than a separate long prelims section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omit detailed experimental protocols from main 12 pages; cite methods instead
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid lengthy procedural descriptions (e.g., step-by-step experimental protocols) in the page-limited Research Strategy; instead describe experiments at a level sufficient for evaluation and cite published methods for details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves space for rationale, aims, and key results. If reviewers need detail, provide enough to evaluate rigor and feasibility or place details in allowed supplemental/sectional areas (e.g., Vertebrate Animals) while ensuring the main narrative remains intelligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide statistical justification for animal numbers and experimental design
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify animal group sizes and experimental design statistically (power/justification), especially when using vertebrate animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters reported placing statistical justifications in the Vertebrate Animals section (e.g., number per group calculations). Make sure the justification is explicit and matches the described aims so reviewers are satisfied with sample size and design choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be economical and selective with figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use figures sparingly and strategically (examples: one intro/overview/background schematic in Significance; 1–2 data figures per aim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fewer, high-impact figures that directly support the aims are preferred. Some writers reduced number of figures relative to older 25-page proposals to fit the shorter format while preserving key evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t assume reviewers will find moved content; make critical points visible
rubrics_metrics.description: If you place material outside the main Research Strategy, do not assume all reviewers will read those sections; critical information placed elsewhere may be missed or cause reviewer irritation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If essential to evaluation, include a concise pointer or summary in the main text so a reviewer can understand without hunting. Several commenters warned that reviewers may skim extraneous sections and some may penalize hidden content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use permitted supplements or late updates sparingly to supply new preliminary data
rubrics_metrics.description: Where allowed (e.g., by agency mechanisms such as SRA permission), submit a concise 1–2 page supplementary data update prior to review to include the latest preliminary results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can provide a 'taste' of newest data for reviewers, but only if agency rules permit. Keep supplemental material concise and directly tied to the aims; do not use supplements to reintroduce bulk that should have been integrated into the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep preliminary data tightly linked to proposed experiments (avoid irrelevant prelims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include only those preliminary studies that directly support the proposed experiments and the logic of each aim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using prelims as selective rationale shortens the application and helps non-expert reviewers digest the proposal. Commenters recommended avoiding prelims that are not directly informative for the requested work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check page-count rules for Specific Aims and other elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm which pages are counted toward the Research Strategy limit (one commenter noted Specific Aims may not be counted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency instructions and FOA-specific guidance determine counting; verify current rules so you can allocate space appropriately (e.g., whether Specific Aims are included in the 12-page Research Strategy).
